verifications.claim: Appendicitis is a medical emergency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "It is a medical emergency." (R2); "Appendicitis is a medical emergency." (R6, R14); multiple sources repeat this phrase.
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated in numerous references as a medical emergency due to rupture risk.

verifications.claim: Appendicitis is caused by an inflamed appendix.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "Appendicitis is a painful swelling and infection of the appendix." (R2); "Appendicitis is an inflammation of the appendix." (R3, R12).
verifications.reasoning: Appendicitis is defined as the inflammation itself, not caused by it; claim reverses the definition.

verifications.claim: Appendicitis is usually triggered by a blockage.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Appendicitis happens when the inside of the appendix is blocked by something" (R2); "A blockage inside of the appendix causes appendicitis" (R5).
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported as primary trigger in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Appendicitis results in sudden, severe abdominal pain that often moves from the belly button to the lower-right abdomen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "May start in the area around the bellybutton, and move to the lower right-hand side of the belly" (R2); classic migration described identically.
verifications.reasoning: Precise match to classic symptom presentation.

verifications.claim: Vomiting is a symptom of appendicitis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Upset stomach (nausea) and vomiting" (R2, R6, R7).

verifications.claim: Loss of appetite is a symptom of appendicitis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Loss of appetite" (R2, R3, R5).

verifications.claim: Abdominal tenderness is a symptom of appendicitis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "McBurney’s point is the most typical location... tenderness there" (R3); rebound tenderness.
verifications.reasoning: Physical exam finding of tenderness directly stated.

verifications.claim: Pain of appendicitis often begins around the belly button.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "May start in the area around the bellybutton" (R2).

verifications.claim: Pain of appendicitis shifts to the lower right abdomen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "move to the lower right-hand side of the belly" (R2).

verifications.claim: Pain of appendicitis worsens with movement, coughing, or walking.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "May be worse when the child is moving... coughing and sneezing" (R2).

verifications.claim: Nausea is a symptom of appendicitis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Upset stomach (nausea)" (R2).

verifications.claim: Constipation is a symptom of appendicitis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Trouble having a bowel movement (constipation)" (R2).

verifications.claim: Diarrhea is a symptom of appendicitis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Loose stool (diarrhea)" (R2); "Diarrhea" (R3).

verifications.claim: Low-grade fever is a symptom of appendicitis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Fever and chills" (R2); "Low-grade fever" (R12).

verifications.claim: Abdominal bloating is a symptom of appendicitis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Swollen belly" (R2); "Swollen belly in younger children" (R7).

verifications.claim: Inability to pass gas is a symptom of appendicitis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "can’t pass gas" (R3); "Inability to pass gas" (R5).

verifications.claim: Pain of appendicitis may differ in children or during pregnancy.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Kids... pregnant may be less likely to present with typical symptoms" (R3); "pain may seem to be in the upper abdomen during pregnancy" (R8).
verifications.reasoning: Sources note atypical presentation in children and pregnancy.

verifications.claim: Hardened stool (fecaliths) is the most common cause of appendicitis.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "Hardened poop (appendix stones)... likely to cause inflammation" (R3); "often by poop" (R10).
verifications.reasoning: Listed as common cause of blockage, but not explicitly 'most common'; other causes like lymphoid hyperplasia also prominent.

verifications.claim: Fecaliths block the opening of the appendix.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "get stuck in the opening to your appendix" (R3).

verifications.claim: Lymphoid hyperplasia is a cause of blockage leading to appendicitis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Lymphoid hyperplasia... can obstruct it and lead to infection" (R3).

verifications.claim: Lymphoid hyperplasia is swollen lymphoid tissue.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "lymphoid tissue in your appendix to swell" (R3).

verifications.claim: Lymphoid hyperplasia often follows a viral infection.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "response to a virus or infection" (R3); "after they have a cold" (R9).
verifications.reasoning: Supported as response to infection, often viral, but 'often follows' is broader.

verifications.claim: Colitis or tumors are other sources of obstruction or infection leading to appendicitis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Colitis... affect your appendix" (R3); "Sometimes tumors can cause appendicitis" (R6).

verifications.claim: Obstruction of the appendix causes bacteria to multiply.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "germs (bacteria) in the appendix begin to increase quickly" (R2).

verifications.claim: Obstruction of the appendix leads to swelling.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "makes it swell up" (R6); "leads to increased pressure... inflammation" (R5).

verifications.claim: Obstruction of the appendix leads to pus.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "pus and other fluids" (R1); appendix fills with pus implied in progression.

verifications.claim: Obstruction of the appendix can lead to rupture.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The appendix will burst or rupture" (R2).

verifications.claim: Physical exam for appendicitis checks for pain in the lower right abdomen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "tenderness there [McBurney’s point] is the first thing" (R3).

verifications.claim: Blood and urine tests for appendicitis check for infection or pregnancy.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Blood tests... check for infection"; "Urine test... bladder or kidney infection" (R2); pregnancy test in R10.
verifications.reasoning: Blood for infection, urine rules out UTI/pregnancy; directly supported.

verifications.claim: Abdominal ultrasound is commonly used to confirm inflammation in appendicitis diagnosis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Abdominal ultrasound... used to see internal organs" (R2).

verifications.claim: CT scan is commonly used to confirm inflammation in appendicitis diagnosis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "CT scan... detailed images" (R2); "one of the most accurate" (R9).

verifications.claim: Appendicitis is most common in people aged 10–30.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "between the ages of 10 and 30 years" (R2).

verifications.claim: Appendicitis is slightly more common in males.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "occurs more frequently in males than females" (R4); "8.6% of biologically male... 6.7% female" (R8).

verifications.claim: Family history of appendicitis can increase risk.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Having a family history of appendicitis may also increase a child’s risk" (R2); study shows OR 2.9 (R11).

verifications.claim: Appendectomy is the standard treatment for appendicitis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Surgery to remove the appendix is called an appendectomy. It is the most common type of emergency surgery" (R2).

verifications.claim: Appendectomy is surgery to remove the appendix.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the appendix be removed with an operation" (R1).

verifications.claim: Antibiotics are sometimes used for appendicitis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "your child may receive antibiotics"; "give antibiotics instead of surgery" (R2).

verifications.claim: Surgery is preferred to prevent rupture in appendicitis treatment.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "advise that your child have surgery to remove the appendix" to prevent burst (R2).

verifications.claim: An infected appendix can rupture in 48–72 hours if left untreated.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "as soon as 48 to 72 hours after you start having symptoms" (R6); exact timeframe.

verifications.claim: Rupture spreads infection in the abdomen (peritonitis).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "causing a severe, life-threatening infection"; "peritonitis may occur" (R2).

verifications.claim: Peritonitis can be fatal.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "If not treated, it can be fatal" (R2); leads to sepsis.
